# Independent audit: exhaustive convex partition with integer centroids

Audited both `candidate 7e12497595d939f1` and
`candidate edf02845b3275e8c` in full, including
their combined theorem. Result: **PASS**; no correction identified.

## Finite target compression

The fractional assignment polytope is nonempty and compact. Every
row's mass and integer first moment have the stated constraints.
The merging operation removes an epsilon-lambda share proportionally
from each positive row and adds the combined source vector to the
integer average target. It preserves each source column and every
row mean. This remains true if the receiving target is itself one
of the rows from which mass is removed. Sufficiently small epsilon
keeps all entries nonnegative. The strictly negative change in the
squared-target-norm objective is the exact weighted variance formula.

Consequently no nontrivial convex combination of positive target
indices can be an integer. This excludes both nonvertices among
the positive targets and additional integer points in their convex
hull. The parity bound follows directly in the original Z^n; no
lattice-changing coordinate transformation is used. For n=0 there
is one possible target. The argument counts target barycenters,
not the number of source fibers in any class.

For intrinsic q≥1, the positive-q-fiber base set is indeed lattice
convex. Any integer Minkowski average has dimension at least q
and at most the original maximal integer-fiber dimension q.
Compact convexity then gives positive finite q-volume. This works
without assuming a common direction space for the original fibers.

## Simultaneous convex realization

The feasible class-moment set is exactly the stated Minkowski sum
of simplices. Discarding zero-mass labels loses no source mass,
since all their nonnegative assignments must be zero. Pairwise
generic continuous score differences can be fixed in advance,
even for varying intrinsic direction spaces. They make every
score-tie set null for H_q on each positive fiber.

The max-score hinge is continuously differentiable with the stated
winner-moment gradient. Its bounded difference from the support
function is uniform in all score parameters. For a relative-interior
target, this gives coercivity on the exact affine direction space
U. Since the gradient and target lie in the same feasible polytope,
restricted gradient vanishing gives the full desired equality.
Neither redundant common-score gauges nor dependent base
coordinates introduce a missing stationarity equation.

For a boundary target, exposing its smallest polytope face yields
precisely the allowed-label sets I_z in the source summands. The
restricted hinge has the same null-tie and bounded-error properties,
and its gradient takes values in that face. Relative-interior
minimization therefore works in span(F−F), including a singleton
face. Adding a sufficiently large finite exposing score makes
every disallowed label strictly lose on its compact source fiber.
There are finitely many fibers and labels, so one finite value
works simultaneously. This is exact saturation, not a passage to
an infinite-score partition or a discarded boundary mass.

The final closed affine winner cells are intersections of C with
at most k−1 halfspaces. A finite maximum exists at every point of
the full ambient C, so they cover ALL of C, including real-base
points and original zero-q-volume fibers. Pairwise cell overlaps
are contained in the null score-tie sets on the positive fibers;
lower-dimensional fibers contribute zero H_q mass.

Every retained cell has positive intrinsic mass and therefore has
a strict winning point away from all ties. Full ambient interior
points of C approximate that point while preserving its strict
inequalities. Thus every retained cell is an actual full ambient
convex body, not merely a lower-dimensional convex piece. Its
mixed intrinsic dimension is exactly q, and its own H_q measure
agrees with the original restricted measure. Its true centroid
belongs to that compact convex cell. An integer prescribed base
mean consequently places the centroid in its own mixed set.

## Combined conclusion and scope

Using only the positive compressed target labels gives at most
2^n actual convex polyhedral pieces, exhaustive on all C, with
pairwise H_q-null mixed overlaps. Their distinct true integer-base
centroids form the vertex set of an empty lattice polytope. No
additional zero-mass cells need to be removed from the cover.

The binary-product sharpness example is valid: an integer mean at
a binary vertex forces every source coordinate to equal that
vertex coordinate almost surely, so each positive vertex fiber
needs its own class even before geometric realization. The q=0
purification exclusion is necessary and properly maintained.

The construction is a simultaneous affine-score partition and
does not imply a recursive sequence of single hyperplane cuts.
It supplies no continuous Grunbaum inequality for the intrinsic
mixed measure of a piece and therefore is not, by itself, an OC
proof. No measure, lattice, or boundary gap was found.
